doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The recording ban, singers and the stars of Lunceford's band
summary: He says singers rose in the ban and names Lunceford's Joe Thomas, Willie Smith and Freddie Webster.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: This World War II thing, did it just so happen that this recording ban happened around the same time as that?

Yeah. When you couldn’t record? That caused a lot of stuff to go down. That when singers came to the fore, because back when I was a kid, we’d go see the big bands. They’d always have some singers that would sit on the side. They might sing two numbers a night. One. Nobody cared, because we’re all there to see Pres and all the cats in Duke’s band. We’d see Ben Webster. Lunceford’s band, we went to hear certain cats. All the bands we had certain cats that we all wanted to hear, and the ladies wanted to hear them too.
Who were the top cats in Lunceford’s band? Just as an aside.
It was Joe – what was his last name? Joe Thomas was his saxophone player, and Willie Smith was the lead alto player.
Those were two, and then he had Webster playing trumpet. We were all crazy about him.
That’s the cat that Miles said he was influenced by.
